title: Zcash Cofounder Launches AI Race to Crack Foundational Cryptographic Hashes
summary:
Zooko Wilcox has partnered with Yukon Research and other labs to crowdsource attacks on the mathematical functions used in current and post-quantum cryptography. The new initiative, called HashSmash, invites participants to use artificial intelligence agents and mathematical expertise to identify vulnerabilities in hashing schemes including SHA-256, SHA-3, and BLAKE3. Multiple users attempted to challenge the security of SHA-3 and BLAKE3 within 23 minutes of the project going live.

The project is a collaboration between the Zcash cofounder and organizations including Eigen Labs, Shielded Labs, and Project Eleven. Sreeram Kannan of Yukon stated the open research challenge was created because AI methods are increasingly capable of breaking cybersecurity. The participants will test if foundational cryptographic schemes that protect the internet remain secure against evolving AI models.

BIG DAY TODAY: https://t.co/fcQoGysos2 is launching today on @yukonresearch.

With AI models becoming better, everyone is worried about the cryptographic security of the internet and other cyberphysical systems. 

Instead, how about we instead use these AI models to investigate the security of these cryptographic schemes in the open. 

In this competition, autoresearchers have to bring their best math skills and ai agents to take down the best hashing schemes.

The instrument of fear instead becomes the tool for our progress. 

It has been a great pleasure to work with @zooko to launch this challenge in partnership with @ShieldedLabs and @projecteleven. 

Smash the Hash!
